sources.title: Wolfgang Soergel, Kategorie O, perverse Garben und Moduln ueber den Koinvarianten zur Weylgruppe, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 3 (1990) 421-445 (MPIM preprint 1989/46, complete German text)
sources.locator: Abstract and Sections 1.1-1.2 (preprint pp. 1-6), Section 2.5 Theorem 11 (preprint p. 18) and Section 2.6 Lemma 10 with Theorem 12 (preprint pp. 18-19); the passages carrying the dot action w.mu = w(mu+rho)-rho, the coinvariant algebra C, the Soergel functor V, Struktursatz 2, Endomorphismensatz 3, Theorem 4, Lemma 10 and Theorem 11 were read in full; the complete 32-page texts of the introduction and Sections 2.5-2.6 were inspected

contents.name: Section 1.1, Zerlegungssatz 1 and the Hecke-algebra action on the split Grothendieck group of the graded C-bimodules (E(t)=<C[-1]>, E(C_s)=<C tensor_{C^s} C>[1], E(C_x)=<B_x>)
Section 1.1, the graded self-dual modules D_x = B_x tensor_C C and their characters, with D_e = C and D_{w_0} = C[l(w_0)]
Section 1.1, Remark 2 to the Zerlegungssatz: the modules D_x are graded and this grading is the 'gemischte Struktur' of category O, an auxiliary datum rather than a grading of O
Section 1.2, the antidominant projective P and the functor V = Hom_g(P,-): O -> mod-End_g(P)
Section 1.2, Struktursatz 2: V induces an isomorphism Hom_g(M,Q) = Hom_{End(P)}(VM,VQ) for all M and projective Q

Section 1.2, Proposition 1 (multiplication Z -> End_g P is surjective) and Endomorphismensatz 3 (End_g P(w_0.lambda) = C^{W_lambda}, kernel = Ann P(w_0.lambda)), with the remark that Bernstein proved it for regular lambda
Section 1.2, Theorem 4: V P(x^{-1}.lambda) = D_x, the left-module/right-reduction convention, and the projective dictionary V P(w.lambda) = reduction of B_{w^{-1}}
Section 1.2, Remark 1 to Theorem 4: End_C(direct sum of the D_x) is the finite-dimensional algebra of category O, an ungraded description of the block
Section 1.2, Remark 5 to Theorem 4: the theorem is 'elementarily equivalent' to the conjectures of Kazhdan and Lusztig

Section 2.5, Theorem 11: a natural equivalence of Z-categories O_lambda(g,b) -> O_lambda'(g',b') for an isomorphism of Coxeter systems, with L(x.lambda) -> L(x'.lambda') and Verma modules corresponding afterwards; and the abstract claim that the structure of the summands of O depends only on the integral Weyl group and the singularity of the central character
contents.reason: The categorical equivalence is strictly stronger than the numerical multiplicity transport proved on this page: it presents each block through its projective-generator endomorphism algebra, and no local Morita/module-category presentation is scaffolded; the numerical answer is obtained directly from the per-block theorem instead, so the equivalence is recorded as known background only.

contents.name: Section 2.6, Lemma 10(i): [P(x^{-1}.0)] = C_x(1)[M(0)] in the Grothendieck group of O_0, proved from the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjectures; the coefficient of y in C_x(1) is the value at t=1 of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial
Section 2.6, Lemma 10(ii)-(iii): <V P(x^{-1}.0)> = C_x(1)<C> and V P(x^{-1}.0) is directly indecomposable
Section 2.6, Theorem 12 and its Lemma: W-actions on <O_0> and on <C-mod> with sM = theta_s M - M and V W-equivariant
Section 2.6, the map c: <P_0> -> Z[W], c(P) = sum_x [P : M(x^{-1}.0)] x, and its identification with the class map on projectives

sources.title: Lin Chen, lecture notes (Spring 2024), Lecture 8: Hecke algebras and the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture (complete 10-page lecture)
sources.locator: Sections 1, 3 and 4 (printed pp. 1-9), namely the Hecke algebra and Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture, contragredient duality on O and the construction of projective covers; the complete lecture text was read

contents.name: Conjecture 1.1: in the principal block O_0 the multiplicities [M_lambda:L_mu] are calculated from Hecke-algebra combinatorics
Definition 1.2 and Warning 1.3: the Hecke algebra with (delta_s - v^{-1})(delta_s + v) = 0 and the dictionary with the (delta_s - q)(delta_s + 1) = 0 convention
Proposition-Definition 1.4, Remark 1.5 and Exercise 1.6: the standard basis delta_w, its independence of the reduced expression, the v=1 specialization recovering ZW, and the multiplication rules
Remark 1.7, Lemma 1.8: the inversion formulas delta_w^{-1} = ... mod lower terms and the algorithm for multiplication in the standard basis
Definition 1.9: the Kazhdan-Lusztig bar involution with bar(delta_s) = delta_s^{-1} and bar(v) = v^{-1}

Theorem-Definition 1.10, Convention 1.11 and Examples 1.12-1.13: existence and uniqueness of the self-dual degree-bounded basis b_w = delta_w + sum h_{w',w} delta_{w'} with h in vZ[v], and the rank-one computation b_s = delta_s + v
Remark 1.14: the pointer to the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of sl_3 in the book of Elias-Makisumi-Thiel-Williamson (Section 3.3.1)
contents.reason: This is a bibliographic pointer rather than a mathematical result, and the book itself is not held; the S_3 polynomials are instead computed from the local triangular construction and cross-checked against the Bjoerner-Brenti computation on printed page 135.

contents.name: Conjecture 1.15: [M_{w'.0}:L_{w.0}] = h_{w',w}(1) for all w,w' in W in the principal block
Remark 1.16: [M_{w'.0}:L_{w.0}] != 0 iff w.0 <= w'.0 in the dominance order, equivalently w >= w' in the Bruhat order

Remarks 1.17-1.18: the conjecture only uses the value at v=1 although that value requires the deformation, and the standard/KL basis elements should be viewed as the incarnations of Verma/simple modules
Conjecture 1.19 and Remark 1.20: positivity of the Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients, known for finite Weyl groups and later for all Coxeter groups by Elias-Williamson
Construction 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Corollary 3.3 and Constructions 3.4-3.7: the dual weight module, the Cartan involution tau and the contragredient duality M^vee = tau(M^{*wt})

Theorem 3.9, Proposition 3.10, Corollary 3.11, Definition 3.12 and Corollary 3.13: contragredient duality is an exact involution on O fixing the L_lambda and the blocks, and dual Verma modules have simple socle L_lambda
Lemma 3.14, Remark 3.15 and Lemma 3.16: dim Hom(M_lambda, M_mu^vee) = delta_{lambda,mu} and Ext^1(M_lambda, M_mu^vee) = 0
Example 3.17: for sl_2 the duality classification M_l = L_l or the nonsplit sequence 0 -> L_l -> M_l^vee -> L_{-l-2} -> 0
Theorem 4.3: O has enough projectives and injectives
Theorem 4.4 with its appendix proof: existence, uniqueness and labelling of projective covers, and dim Hom(P_lambda,M) = [M:L_lambda]
Corollary 4.9 and Exercise 4.12: dim Hom_O(P_lambda,M) = [M:L_lambda] and the comparison of the representing object with the projective cover
Lemma 4.10 and Remark 4.11: the lambda-weight functor on a block is representable, by M_lambda when lambda is dot-dominant

sources.locator: Section 5.1 (printed pp. 133-136) on the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, their existence/uniqueness theorem, the R-polynomial recursion and the S_3 and S_4 computations; Section 5.5 (printed pp. 153-158, consulted for the nonrecursive formulas); and the exercises to Chapter 5 (printed pp. 163-165, Exercise 7(a) and Exercise 12); the complete relevant passages were read

contents.name: Theorem 5.1.4: existence and uniqueness of the family P_{u,v}(q) with constant term 1, degree and parity bounds and the descent recursion
Proposition 5.1.5: P_{u,v}(0) = 1 for u <= v
The explicit S_3 computation on printed p. 135: P_{u,321}(q) = 1 for all u != 123 and P_{123,321}(q) = 1, so every Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of S_3 equals 1
The S_4 examples on printed p. 135: P_{2134,4231}(q) = P_{1324,3412}(q) = 1 + q
Definition (5.3) of the mu-coefficient as the coefficient of q^{(l(u,w)-1)/2} for odd length differences and 0 otherwise
Theorem 5.1.7: the full descent recursion with the mu-correction sum
Exercises 7(a) and 12 on printed pp. 163-165: P_{u,v} = 1 whenever the length difference is at most two, and P_{u,v}(q) = P_{u^{-1},v^{-1}}(q)
Theorem 5.5.2 and the nonrecursive formula of Section 5.5 (printed pp. 153-158) expressing P_{u,v} through chains and R-polynomials
contents.reason: The nonrecursive chain formula is a general-purpose computational device for arbitrary Coxeter groups; this page's finite examples are short enough that the local descent recursion already gives the polynomials, so the longer formula is not scaffolded or used.

contents.name: Section 6.2, the coloured Kazhdan-Lusztig graph and the S_3 cell picture used for the cell-theoretic classification

contents.name: Example 1.13: b_s = delta_s + v and h_{id,s} = v, the rank-one Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial

sources.locator: Sections 1-3 (printed pp. 1-7): standard filtrations, BGG reciprocity, translation functors and facets; in particular Definition 3.8-3.9, Example 3.11, Theorem 3.12, Theorem 3.13, Examples 3.15-3.16; complete passages read

contents.name: Example 3.11: for sl_2 the facets (-infinity,-1), {-1}, (-1,infinity) in the coordinate l = <lambda,alpha^vee>
Theorem 3.12 and its sketch: T_lambda^mu(M_{w.lambda}) = M_{w.mu}, the dual Verma case, and T_lambda^mu(L_{w.lambda}) = L_{w.mu} or 0 according to the upper closure condition
Example 3.16: for sl_2 the equivalence O_{w(0)} ~= O_{w(l)} for l in Z_{>=0} sends 0 -> M_{-2} -> M_0 -> L_0 -> 0 to 0 -> M_{-l-2} -> M_l -> L_l -> 0
Theorem 3.13 and Example 3.15: translation functors inside a facet are equivalences, and every dot-regular integral block is equivalent to the principal block preserving Verma and simple modules
contents.reason: The equivalence is a categorical statement whose source argument is a sketch relying on Humphreys Section 7; this page only needs and proves the numerical coincidence of the multiplicity matrices, which is obtained from the per-block multiplicity theorem without any equivalence.
